sources_considered.why: Read the original Salesforce paper, including its methods, failures and stronger workflow results.
Independent primary evaluation of multistep tasks. Only the original March 2025 discussion is used.
Primary evaluation and architectural ablations provide counterevidence to an unavoidable reliability barrier, with substantial vendor-study limitations.
The original research paper is more direct than the company's later explanatory article.

evidence_items.locator: Results discussion, paragraph following the heading about acquiring information through clarification
evidence_items.explanation: Supports the narrower reliability concern: overall success fell from approximately 58% to 35% when agents needed conversational clarification. The same paper reports over 83% success for some workflow-execution tasks, so its findings do not establish universal unworkability.

evidence_items.locator: Summary, paragraph beginning Current frontier AIs
evidence_items.explanation: Supports contemporary concerns about sustained autonomous work. The study also finds high success on short tasks and improving capabilities; it does not establish an inherent ceiling.

The developer reports 91.25% success on SpreadsheetBench and 75.2% single-attempt success on GAIA, with gains from system architecture and specialized models. This challenges the inference from model fallibility to system impossibility, but independent replication and deployment-wide reliability are not established.

unresolved_gaps: The evidence establishes important failures but not that model unreliability necessarily makes agents unworkable.
The strongest architectural counterexample examined is developer-reported and does not establish dependable performance across representative production workflows.
No task scope or practical reliability requirement is specified.
